The main takeaway from our work is that

, when dealing with simulation, the proof of a preservation result for a logic L boils down to showing that the set of formulas of L which can be expressed by a given formula ψ in L is closed under the operation of replacing all occurrences of ψ in a formula of L by an arbitrary formula of L.

, in the case of simulation-based proofs of property preservation for a wide range of temporal and modal logics, the main difficulty is not the logic itself, but the fact that the proof must be carried out in the context of an infinite-state model checker.
